Internal helper: a target format given where jconvert() takes variables

Source: R/recode.R
dot-jst_convert_target_pointer.Rd

Until v0.9.227 to was jconvert()'s second formal, so jconvert(d, Education) bound Education to to: R's "object 'Education' not found", or, with a workspace object of that name, its value taken as the target and the whole frame converted (Session 354, ruling A of the S243 item). The dots are second now, as in every data-first function, and the target is always named – as every printed line names it. This check gives the old positional form the line to run: a format name typed in quotes or bare (jconvert(d, "stata"), jconvert(d, stata)), or a name holding one (fmt <- "stata"; jconvert(d, fmt)), stops with the call rebuilt as jconvert(d, <the other variables>, to = "stata"), keeping modify = TRUE when the call had it. A name the data frame has is a variable, whatever it is called.

Usage

.jst_convert_target_pointer(variables, data, data_name, modify)

Arguments

variables

The quosures of ..., after the juse() prepend.

data

The resolved data frame.

data_name

Its name, for the line.

modify

The call's modify flag.

Value

Invisible NULL; stops when a target format is found.
